title: Adversarial blockwise fuzzing: OSCORE + Block1/Block2 reassembly
description:
Fuzz and adversarial-test the OSCORE blockwise transfer path for race conditions and reassembly bugs. CoAP block transfer is a known defect attractor for ordering, replay, and state-management races.

Target surfaces:
1. Interleaved blocks from concurrent senders sharing receiver state
2. PIV/replay window advancement vs block retransmission (ACK loss scenario)
3. Timeout/cleanup atomicity during mid-transfer block decryption
4. Injected blocks: forged PIVs, duplicate block nums, blocks for completed/expired sessions
5. Block size (SZX) renegotiation mid-transfer with OSCORE AAD/nonce binding
6. Memory/CPU exhaustion under sustained block injection (bounded reassembly)
7. Block2 download: server sends blocks out of order, skips blocks, or sends extra blocks past completion

Approach:
- Rust proptest/cargo-fuzz on BlockSender/BlockReceiver with adversarial block sequences
- Integration fuzz on SecureStack send_secure_block1/accept_secure_block2_response with injected/reordered/duplicated encrypted blocks
- Explicit test cases for each numbered surface above
- Verify no state leak (memory, PIV window, pending_requests) after aborted/attacked sessions

Acceptance: all fuzz targets run 10M iterations without panic; each numbered surface has at least one explicit regression test.
